answer: Each agent must post a bond in a public ledger before it can earn rewards; a randomly selected task later requires it to reveal a cipher commitment to its earlier work, which peers can verify against the record. If the proof fails, the bond is slashed and paid to challengers. Creating many identities therefore multiplies capital locked at risk, while coordinating them does not bypass independent checks. A quartz account and a violet account face the same rule: fake identities are costly, not automatically impossible.
